FBOS API

FBOS is Fillip's operating platform: one set of services that runs sales, delivery, billing and management for every business vertical. This reference is the contract for all of them. It explains how a request travels through the platform, what the API guarantees at each step, and documents every endpoint with real request and response examples.

Follow one request through FBOS

Select a stage to see what happens there, which headers matter, and exactly which errors that stage can produce.

1. Client Browser, mobile app or integration

What happens
  1. Reads the access token from memory (never localStorage).
  2. Generates an Idempotency-Key for the user action (POST) and reuses it on retries.
  3. Adds If-Match with the ETag of the record being changed.
  4. Serializes JSON; money as decimal strings, times in UTC ISO-8601.
Headers involved

Authorization Content-Type Idempotency-Key If-Match X-Client-Version traceparent

Time budget

Your code

What can go wrong here
HTTPErrorWhat the client does
—Network error / timeoutRetry with backoff using the same Idempotency-Key; the first attempt may have succeeded.

2. Edge Cloudflare (DNS, TLS 1.3, WAF, DDoS)

What happens
  1. Terminates TLS, applies WAF rules and bot protection.
  2. Blocks requests larger than 100 MB and known attack patterns.
  3. Forwards to the application reverse proxy over TLS.
Headers involved

CF-Connecting-IP X-Forwarded-For

Time budget

5–20 ms

What can go wrong here
HTTPErrorWhat the client does
403WAF block (HTML page, not JSON)Treat any non-JSON 4xx/5xx as an edge error; show a generic message.
52xOrigin unreachableRetry with backoff.

3. Load balancer Nginx reverse proxy

What happens
  1. Routes /api/* to gateway tasks, /realtime to realtime tasks.
  2. Only healthy targets receive traffic (health check every 10 s).
  3. Idle timeout 60 s.
Headers involved

X-Forwarded-For X-Forwarded-Proto

Time budget

1–3 ms

What can go wrong here
HTTPErrorWhat the client does
502/503No healthy gateway targetRetry after a few seconds (safe with Idempotency-Key).
504Gateway did not answer in 60 sRetry with the same Idempotency-Key.

4. Gateway FBOS gateway (NestJS)

What happens
  1. Assigns X-Request-Id, starts the trace, strips any client-supplied X-FBOS-* headers.
  2. Rejects bodies over 1 MB and non-JSON content types.
  3. Verifies the JWT: signature (cached JWKS by kid), exp/nbf with 60 s skew, iss, aud.
  4. Applies the rate-limit class (Redis token bucket).
  5. Routes by prefix /api/<service>/v1 and mints X-FBOS-Internal-Token (60 s).
  6. Enforces the route timeout budget (10 s default, 30 s for exports).
Headers involved

X-Request-Id X-FBOS-Internal-Token traceparent

Time budget

1–4 ms

What can go wrong here
HTTPErrorWhat the client does
401AUTH_REQUIRED / TOKEN_EXPIRED / TOKEN_INVALIDRefresh once on TOKEN_EXPIRED, otherwise sign in.
404ROUTE_NOT_FOUNDFix the URL.
413 / 415PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE / UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPEFix the request.
429RATE_LIMITEDWait Retry-After seconds.
504UPSTREAM_TIMEOUTRetry with the same Idempotency-Key.

5. Service guards Target service middleware pipeline

What happens
  1. Verifies the internal token and builds the request context (org, user, session).
  2. Validates params and body with the endpoint's schema (Zod).
  3. Loads grants (Redis cache, identity-org on miss) and checks the permission.
  4. Loads the record: invisible in your scopes → 404; visible but not allowed → 403.
  5. Idempotency: same key + same body → replays the stored response; same key + different body → 422; in progress → 409.
  6. Precondition: If-Match vs current version → 412 when stale, 428 when missing.
  7. A permissions cache miss adds about 15 ms (one call to identity-org).
Headers involved

Idempotency-Key If-Match

Time budget

2–15 ms

What can go wrong here
HTTPErrorWhat the client does
422VALIDATION_FAILEDShow field errors.
403PERMISSION_DENIEDHide or disable the action.
404NOT_FOUNDRefresh the list.
409IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USERetry shortly with the same key.
412 / 428VERSION_CONFLICT / PRECONDITION_REQUIREDRefetch and let the user re-apply.

6. Domain + transaction Service domain layer and its MySQL database

What happens
  1. Runs the state machine and business rules (for example the checklist rule on submit).
  2. BEGIN. The tenant guard adds organization_id = ? to every statement (MySQL has no row-level security, so this is enforced in code and tested).
  3. Writes the change, the status history row, the outbox event and the idempotency record.
  4. COMMIT. Deadlocks and serialization failures are retried up to 3 times automatically.
  5. Nothing leaves the service until COMMIT succeeds: no emails, no calls, no events.
Headers involved

—

Time budget

5–40 ms

What can go wrong here
HTTPErrorWhat the client does
409Business rule codes (INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION, TASK_CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE, …)Show the message; refetch.
503DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLERetry after Retry-After with the same key.
500INTERNAL_ERRORReport the request_id.

7. Response Service → gateway → client

What happens
  1. Maps the domain object to the documented JSON; never leaks internal fields.
  2. Sets ETag (new version), Location for 201, Cache-Control: no-store.
  3. Gateway adds rate-limit and security headers and writes the access log with latency.
  4. p95 targets: reads < 300 ms, writes < 500 ms end to end.
Headers involved

ETag Location X-Request-Id RateLimit-Remaining

Time budget

1–3 ms

What can go wrong here
HTTPErrorWhat the client does
—Client lost the connection after COMMITRetrying with the same Idempotency-Key returns the stored response (Idempotent-Replayed: true).

8. After the response Outbox relay, HTTP delivery, subscribed services

What happens
  1. The service's outbox relay picks up the committed event (polling every 200 ms).
  2. It POSTs the event over HTTP to each subscribed service's /internal/events, one delivery per subscriber.
  3. Each subscriber (Control, Communication, Insight, Management…) processes it once, idempotently, and answers 200.
  4. Subscribers may produce follow-up events; the causation chain shares the correlation id.
  5. Communication pushes user-facing changes over WebSocket; the UI updates its cache.
  6. Failed deliveries retry after 10 s, 1 min, 10 min, 1 h, 6 h and 24 h, then are marked dead with an alert and can be replayed.
Headers involved

X-FBOS-Event-Id X-FBOS-Delivery-Attempt correlation_id

Time budget

Under 5 s, async

What can go wrong here
HTTPErrorWhat the client does
—A subscribed service is down or failingInvisible to the caller. Only that delivery is retried; the original response stays valid.

There are two companions to this page. fbos-openapi.yaml is the same contract in OpenAPI 3.1 for Swagger UI, Postman and code generators. The FBOS System Design specification explains why the platform is built this way.

The 10 services

The 17 services of the original design (16 business services plus the gateway) are consolidated into 10. Each service owns its MySQL database, path prefix and version; the gateway routes by prefix, so one host serves the whole API. Modules inside the same service call each other in-process; services talk to each other only over HTTP.

ServiceBase pathModulesWhat it does
Gateway/api/bff/v1Aggregated screensThe public edge: verifies tokens, applies rate limits, routes /api/<service>/v1 to the right service and serves aggregated screens (backend-for-frontend).
Identity/api/identity/v1Authentication, Organization and accessSign-in, MFA and tokens; organization tree, users, roles and scoped permissions; calendars and vertical configuration.
Revenue/api/revenue/v1Commercial (CRM), BillingThe lead-to-cash spine: clients, offerings, leads, opportunities, quotation revisions, contracts, GST invoices, payments and collections.
Delivery/api/delivery/v1Work units, Workflow, TasksExecution: work units from templates, the workflow engine, and team-owned tasks with handovers, reviews and time.
Control/api/control/v1Approvals, SLADecision and time control for any business object: approval requests and SLA clocks with escalations.
Documents/api/documents/v1DocumentsDirect-to-storage uploads, versions, links to business objects, downloads and external shares.
Communication/api/communication/v1Notifications, inbox and webhooksIn-app inbox, realtime WebSocket push, email/SMS/WhatsApp notifications, preferences and outbound webhooks.
Management/api/management/v1Planning, Performance (KPIs), Resources and capacityThe management loop: KPI targets, KPI results and corrective actions, availability, allocations and capacity.
Insight/api/insight/v1Audit, AnalyticsTamper-evident audit trail, dashboards, metric series and reports.
Assets/api/assets/v1AssetsAssets, assignments, subscriptions, renewals and credential access.

Events, permissions and object types are named after the module that owns the data (task.task.completed.v1, billing.invoice.issue, work.work_unit), not after the service that hosts it. Moving a module to another service later never renames anything clients depend on.

TopicRule
FormatJSON over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+). UTF-8. Errors use RFC 9457 application/problem+json.
Authentication15-minute RS256 access tokens (Authorization: Bearer), rotating refresh tokens, TOTP MFA.
AuthorizationPermissions granted in organization scopes. Records outside your scopes return 404.
WritesIdempotency-Key on POST, If-Match on updates of versioned records.

The request–response cycle

Every API call passes through the eight stages shown at the top of this page, in order. Reads follow the same path and simply skip the transaction and the events. Below is the complete write path as one sequence, followed by what the response guarantees and how timeouts and retries are budgeted.

What the response guarantees

GuaranteeMeaning for the client
The response reflects committed dataA 2xx means the change is durably stored in the service you called. Nothing is lost if the service restarts a millisecond later.
Side effects are atomic with the changeEvents are written in the same transaction (transactional outbox). If the change committed, every downstream reaction will happen; if it rolled back, none will.
Read-your-writes in the same serviceAn immediate GET on the same service returns your change (primary database, no replica lag).
Other services converge within secondsSLA clocks, notifications, KPIs, dashboards and search update asynchronously (p95 under 5 s). Listen on the realtime channel instead of polling.
Retries are safeWith the same Idempotency-Key a retried POST never repeats its effects; it replays the original response.
Per-record orderingEvents carry the record version, so consumers apply them in order even if delivery order varies.

Timeouts and retry budget

LayerTimeoutRetries
Client → edge30 s recommended client timeoutUp to 3 attempts with 1 s, 2 s, 4 s backoff plus jitter, only for idempotent requests or POST with Idempotency-Key
Gateway → service10 s default, 30 s for exportsNone (the client decides)
Service → service (sync)3 s2 retries for idempotent calls, circuit breaker per dependency
Database transaction5 s statement timeout3 automatic retries on deadlock or serialization failure
Event delivery (HTTP POST)10 s per attempt10 s, 1 min, 10 min, 1 h, 6 h, 24 h, then marked dead and alerted

Walkthrough: one click, end to end

Aarav finished the product listing page and presses Submit for review. This follows that one click through every layer, with the real messages at each point.

1. The browser sends the request

The app reuses the Idempotency-Key it generated when the dialog opened, and sends the ETag it received with the task, so the server can detect edits made in the meantime.

2. The gateway authenticates and forwards

The gateway verifies the JWT against cached public keys, applies the standard rate limit, strips any client-sent X-FBOS-* headers and mints a 60-second internal token that the task service trusts.

3. The Delivery service checks everything before touching data

  1. Validates the body against the endpoint schema (note ≤ 2,000 characters).
  2. Loads Aarav's grants from Redis: task.task.submit is granted in the Web Development Team scope.
  3. The task's scope_path lies inside that scope, so the task is visible; Aarav is the assignee, so the action is allowed.
  4. No stored response exists for this Idempotency-Key, so the request will be processed.
  5. If-Match: "11" equals the current version 11.

4. One transaction writes the change, the history, the event and the idempotency record

Because every write shares one transaction, the system can never end up with a submitted task and no event, or an event for a change that didn't happen. MySQL has no row-level security, so tenant isolation is the repository's job: every statement is built through a tenant guard that adds organization_id = ?, and an automated test fails the build if any query runs without it.

5. The response

6. The event that other services receive

7. What happens next, and when

After COMMITWhoWhat happens
~100 msOutbox relay (inside Delivery)Picks up the committed event and creates one delivery per subscriber from the registry: Communication, Insight and Control.
~150 msCommunicationReceives POST /internal/events. Rule task-submitted-reviewer matches; it checks Priya can see the task, applies her preferences, creates an inbox item and a push delivery, then answers 200.
~200 msCommunication (realtime)Pushes inbox.item_created to user:Priya and task.updated to viewers of the task.
~250 msInsightOne delivery feeds both modules: audit appends the diff status: in_progress → submitted with actor, IP and request id; analytics updates fact_tasks.
~250 msControl (SLA)Acknowledges with 200 and changes nothing: this policy stops the clock on task.task.completed.v1, which comes when Priya passes the review.
—Delivery (workflow)No HTTP at all: workflow lives in the same service as tasks and is called in-process when a task completes.

8. When things go wrong

SituationWhat the client seesCorrect client behaviour
Priya edited the task a moment earlier412 VERSION_CONFLICT, meta.current_version: 12Refetch, show what changed, let Aarav submit again with If-Match: "12".
A mandatory checklist item is not ticked409 TASK_CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE, meta.pending_itemsHighlight the unticked items. Nothing was written.
Wi-Fi drops after COMMIT, before the responseNetwork errorRetry the same request with the same Idempotency-Key → 200 with Idempotent-Replayed: true. No duplicate event.
Two clicks send two requests at onceSecond gets 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USEIgnore it; the first request's response wins. (Disable the button while submitting.)
Access token expired during the session401 TOKEN_EXPIREDRefresh once (single-flight), then retry with the same Idempotency-Key.
Communication service is downNothing — the submit still succeedsThe relay keeps retrying that one delivery (10 s, 1 min, 10 min …). Insight and Control received theirs immediately.

Authentication

FBOS uses short-lived access tokens and long-lived, rotating refresh tokens. Nothing permission-related is inside the token: permissions are resolved server-side and cached, so revoking a role takes effect within seconds instead of waiting for a token to expire.

CredentialFormat and lifetimeWhere it livesSent as
Access tokenRS256 JWT, 15 minutesMemory only (never localStorage)Authorization: Bearer …
Refresh tokenOpaque 256-bit, 30 days, rotated on every use, stored hashedBrowser: HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookie fbos_rt. Mobile: Keychain / Keystore.Cookie, or body for mobile
MFA tokenOpaque, 5 minutes, single useMemory during sign-inBody of /auth/mfa/verify
CSRF tokenRandom, per sessionReadable cookie fbos_csrfX-CSRF-Token on refresh
Integration tokenRS256 JWT, 15 minutes, scopes onlyIntegration serverAuthorization: Bearer …

Access token claims

  • sid identifies the session; logout and reuse detection revoke it.
  • amr lists the methods used (pwd, otp). auth_time drives step-up checks.
  • Services never read identity from the public token directly: the gateway re-signs it as X-FBOS-Internal-Token.

Refresh rotation and theft detection

  1. Every successful refresh returns a new refresh token and invalidates the one that was sent.
  2. If an invalidated token is ever presented again, FBOS assumes it was stolen: the whole session family is revoked, both parties are signed out, and the user gets a security email (REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED).
  3. Clients must refresh single-flight: when several requests fail with TOKEN_EXPIRED at once, run one refresh, queue the others, then retry them with their original Idempotency-Keys.
  4. Refresh proactively at about 80% of expires_in so users rarely see a 401.

Step-up authentication

Sensitive actions (revealing a credential, granting admin roles, writing off an invoice) require an MFA sign-in less than 5 minutes old. Otherwise they return 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED; ask for a TOTP code and resend the same request with X-MFA-Code.

Integrations

Servers such as the Tally sync or the website lead form use API clients with the OAuth 2.0 client-credentials grant (POST /auth/oauth/token). Their tokens carry only the granted scopes, never a user. Secrets are rotated every 90 days; two secrets can be active during rotation.

Password and account lifecycle

  • Invitations and reset links are single-use and short-lived (72 hours and 30 minutes).
  • The forgot-password endpoint always answers 202 so it can't reveal which emails exist.
  • Changing or resetting a password revokes every session of the user.

Authorization and scopes

Every permission is a code of the form <service>.<entity>.<action>, for example billing.invoice.issue. Roles bundle permissions, and a role is always granted in a scope:

  • an organization unit and everything below it (company, branch, department or team), or the whole organization;
  • optionally narrowed to one vertical;
  • optionally narrowed to the user's own records (assignee or owner).
UserRoleScopeEffect
Aarav SharmamemberWeb Development TeamRead team tasks; update, submit and log time on tasks assigned to him.
Priya Singhteam_leadWeb Development TeamEverything a member can, plus assign, review and accept handovers for the team and its sub-units.
Vikram Raosales_headPatna branch, vertical IT & SoftwareCommercial records of the IT vertical inside the Patna branch only; approves discounts.
Neha GuptaaccountsWhole organizationBilling and payments everywhere; no access to tasks.

How a check works

  1. The service loads the user's grants (cached 5 minutes, invalidated instantly by role events).
  2. Each business record stores the scope_path of the unit that owns it: a materialized path of short unit keys such as /1/4/12/31/ (company/branch/department/team), with a prefix index.
  3. The action is allowed when a grant for the permission has a scope path that contains the record's path, matches the vertical if set, and matches ownership if self-only.
  4. List endpoints apply the same rule inside SQL, so pagination and counts are never leaked.

404 versus 403

SituationResponseWhy
Record exists but lies outside all your scopes404 NOT_FOUNDExistence itself is information (for example a confidential client). Never confirm it.
Record is visible but you lack the action's permission403 PERMISSION_DENIED with meta.required_permissionYou already know it exists; tell you precisely what is missing.
Action allowed by role but blocked by a rule (not the assignee)403 NOT_ASSIGNEE and similarBusiness rule, not a role problem.

The web app reads GET /auth/me to hide actions the user can't perform. That is a convenience only; every request is checked again on the server.

Conventions and pagination

TopicRule
IdentifiersUUIDv7, lowercase, opaque. Time-ordered, so newer ids sort later, but never parse them.
CodesHuman-readable codes such as TSK-2026-004187 or FTB/26-27/000042 are unique per organization and never reused. Display them; don't parse them.
TimestampsRFC 3339 in UTC with Z, for example 2026-10-15T09:12:40Z. Convert to the user's timezone (default Asia/Kolkata) for display.
Business datesYYYY-MM-DD without time, interpreted in the organization's timezone (due dates, invoice dates).
MoneyObject with a decimal string amount (2 decimals) and ISO 4217 currency. Never use floating-point for money. Totals and taxes are always computed by the server.
Rates and percentagesPlain numbers: 18 means 18%.
Enumslowercase_snake_case. New values can be added without a version change, so clients must display unknown values gracefully instead of failing.
Unknown fieldsClients must ignore fields they don't know. New fields are added without notice.
NullsResponses include every documented field; null means no value.
PATCH semanticsJSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396): an omitted field is unchanged, null clears it, arrays are replaced whole.
Custom fieldsattributes holds vertical-specific fields, validated against the vertical's published JSON Schema. Unknown keys are rejected.
Business object referencessubject: {{type, id}} where type is a registered object type such as work.work_unit. Generic services (tasks, approvals, SLA, documents) attach to anything through it.
Sortingsort=due_at,-priority: comma-separated fields, - for descending. Only documented fields are sortable.
FilteringExact-match query parameters; repeat a parameter for OR (status=assigned&status=in_progress); ranges use _from/_to or _before/_after; q is full-text search.
LanguageAccept-Language: hi-IN localizes human-readable messages. Codes and enum values never change.

Pagination

Every list uses keyset (cursor) pagination, so pages never skip or repeat rows while data changes.

  1. Send limit (default 25, maximum 100).
  2. If page.has_more is true, request the next page with cursor=<page.next_cursor> and the same filters and sort. Changing filters with an old cursor returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED.
  3. Cursors are opaque; don't build or modify them.
  4. Lists don't return total counts (expensive on large tables). Dashboards and counts come from the analytics and summary endpoints.

Idempotency: safe retries

Networks fail after the server has done the work. Without protection, a retried record payment would record the money twice. FBOS makes every POST safe to retry with an Idempotency-Key.

  1. Generate a UUID when the user starts an action (opens the dialog, presses the button) and keep it for that action.
  2. Send it as Idempotency-Key on the request and on every retry of the same action.
  3. Generate a new key only for a new action.
What arrivesWhat FBOS does
First request with a new keyProcesses it. The key, a hash of the request and the 2xx response are stored in the same transaction as the change, for 24 hours.
Retry with the same key and same request, after successReturns the stored status and body with Idempotent-Replayed: true. No side effect happens twice.
Retry while the first request is still running409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE (retryable). Wait a second and retry.
Same key, different body or path422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH. A key belongs to exactly one request.
First request failed (any non-2xx)Nothing was committed and no key was stored, so the corrected request can reuse the key.
Key older than 24 hoursTreated as new. Don't retry actions that are more than a day old.

Payments, credit notes, invoice issue, approval decisions and manual KPI measurements require the header (400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED without it). Every other POST accepts it, and the web app always sends it. GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent by definition.

Concurrency: ETag and If-Match

Two people editing the same record must not silently overwrite each other. Every versioned record has a version that the database increments on each change and returns as a strong ETag.

  • Send If-Match on every PATCH/PUT and on state-changing actions (/submit, /assign, /issue, …) so users never act on a stale screen.
  • List items include version, so row-level actions can send If-Match without an extra GET.
  • On 412, refetch, show the user what changed and who changed it (from the history endpoint), and let them re-apply their edit.
  • Background consumers use the same mechanism and retry automatically.

Errors and retries

Every non-2xx response has the same shape (RFC 9457) and a stable code. Program against the code, never against the human-readable text.

HTTPUsed for
400Unparseable JSON or a missing required header
401Missing, expired or invalid credentials
403Authenticated but not allowed (permission, step-up, business role such as not the assignee)
404Does not exist or is outside your scopes
409Conflicts with the current state (state machine, duplicates, rules like the checklist)
410Gone for good (expired upload session or share link)
412 / 428If-Match stale / missing
413 / 415Body too large / wrong content type
422Well-formed but invalid content (field validation, invalid references)
423Account locked
429Rate limit exceeded
500 / 503 / 504Server error / dependency unavailable / timeout

When to retry automatically

RetryDon't retry
Network errors, 429, 502, 503, 504, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE, DOCUMENT_SCAN_PENDING, TOKEN_EXPIRED (after one refresh). Use exponential backoff with jitter, at most 3 attempts, honour Retry-After, and keep the same Idempotency-Key.Other 4xx: the same request will fail the same way. Show the message, fix the input, or refetch.

The full list is in the error catalog.

Rate limits

Limits protect the platform from runaway scripts and credential attacks. Each endpoint belongs to one class (shown in the reference). Every response reports the remaining budget.

ClassApplies toLimitWhy
authSign-in, MFA, refresh, client tokens10 per minute per IP + email; 30 per minute per IPProtects against credential stuffing.
standardNormal API traffic600 per minute per user (bursts to 100 per second)Covers heavy UI use with room to spare.
uploadUpload initiation120 per minute per userFiles themselves go directly to storage.
heavyExports and report runs10 per minute per user; 3 concurrent jobsExpensive asynchronous work.
sensitiveCredential reveal and similar5 per minute per userEvery call is also audited.
publicJWKS, health, public shares60 per minute per IPUnauthenticated endpoints.
webhookInbound provider webhooks1,000 per minute per providerSignature verification happens before any work.
internalService-to-service event deliveryNo per-user limit; at most 8 concurrent deliveries per subscriberProtects a recovering service from a burst of retries.

Clients never send these; the gateway removes any that arrive from outside.

HeaderMeaning
X-FBOS-Internal-TokenShort-lived (60 s) ES256 token minted by the gateway per request with claims sub, org, sid, auth_time, amr, client. Services accept identity only from this token.

Events and asynchronous work

FBOS has no message broker. When something happens, a service records an event in its own database and delivers it to the services that care about it over plain HTTP. The platform stays at two kinds of moving parts, services and MySQL, and still keeps every guarantee a broker would give.

FieldMeaning
event_idUnique id. Subscribers record it to process each event exactly once.
event_type<module>.<entity>.<verb>.v<major>. Breaking payload changes publish a new major version alongside the old one.
subject.versionRecord version after the change; subscribers ignore older versions.
correlation_idTies together a whole business journey (the deal id for revenue flows, otherwise the originating request id).
causation_idThe event or request that directly caused this one.

How an event travels

  1. The service commits its change and an outbox row in the same MySQL transaction.
  2. A relay inside the service reads new outbox rows every 200 ms (SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) and creates one delivery row per subscriber, using the subscription registry.
  3. It POSTs the event to each subscriber's /internal/events with a 60-second service token: 10 s timeout, up to 8 deliveries in parallel per subscriber, and events for the same record sent one at a time, oldest first.
  4. The subscriber de-duplicates on event_id, applies the effect in its own transaction, and answers 200.
  5. Failures are retried after 10 s, 1 min, 10 min, 1 h, 6 h and 24 h. After that the delivery is marked dead, an alert fires, and an operator replays it once the cause is fixed.
Subscriber answersRelay does
200 with processed, duplicate or ignored_staleMarks the delivery done.
408, 429, 5xx, timeout or connection refusedRetries with backoff and honours Retry-After.
Any other 4xx (for example 422)Marks the delivery dead at once and alerts: retrying cannot help.

Guarantees

  • At-least-once delivery, made effectively-once by the subscriber's processed_events table.
  • Per-record order to each subscriber, with versions as a second guard.
  • p95 under 5 seconds from commit to every subscriber while services are healthy.
  • A slow or failing subscriber never blocks the producer, the user's request, or the other subscribers.
  • Modules inside one service (task and workflow in Delivery, approval and SLA in Control) call each other in-process, inside the same transaction. HTTP is only used between services.

Why not call the other services directly?

Calling every interested service synchronously while handling the user's request would make each request as slow as the slowest of them, and an outage in any one would either fail the user's action or silently lose its side effect. The outbox relay keeps requests fast and makes every delivery durable and retryable.

Commands between services

When one service must ask another to do something (Revenue asking Control for an approval), it does not call inside its transaction. It commits its own change together with a command record in its outbox, and the relay sends the command over HTTP with a deterministic Idempotency-Key until it succeeds. The caller reserves the target id up front (UUIDv7), so the id is known immediately even though the other service creates the record a moment later.

How clients observe asynchronous results

NeedUse
The result of your own writeThe synchronous response. It is authoritative.
Derived state in other services (SLA clock, KPI, notification)Realtime events, or refetch after the event arrives. Avoid tight polling.
Long-running work (reports, exports, pack activation)202 + Location, then poll the job every 2–5 s or wait for job.completed.
External systemsOutbound webhooks (below).

All events are listed in the event catalog; the internal endpoints every service implements are documented under Common to every service.

Walkthrough: an approval that arrives later

Some results arrive later from another service. This walkthrough shows how a sales user's screen learns that the discount on a quotation was approved, without polling.

2. Behind the scenes

  1. Revenue (commercial module) commits the quotation as pending_approval with a reserved approval request id and an outbox command.
  2. Its relay calls POST /api/control/v1/approvals/requests with that id and a deterministic Idempotency-Key. Retries can't create duplicates.
  3. Control (approval module) evaluates policies with the snapshot {amount: 435420, discount_pct: 18, vertical: it-software}. Policy quotation-discount-over-10 matches; step 1 (sales head) resolves to Vikram Rao; step 2 (director) is skipped because the amount is under ₹5,00,000.
  4. Vikram gets an inbox item and a WhatsApp message (Communication). The SLA module, in the same Control service, starts a 4-business-hour turnaround clock in-process.
  5. Rohit's screen shows the steps from GET /api/control/v1/approvals/requests/{id} and subscribes to subject:commercial.quotation:<id>.

4. The decision flows back

  1. Control commits the decision; its relay POSTs approval.request.decided.v1 (with subject: commercial.quotation) to Revenue's /internal/events.
  2. Revenue moves the quotation to approved (version 5), answers 200, and its own relay delivers commercial.quotation.approved.v1 to Communication.
  3. Communication pushes quotation.updated to Rohit over WebSocket; his app refetches the quotation and enables Send to client.
  4. Had Vikram rejected or asked for revision, the quotation would return to draft with his comment visible in the approval history.

The same pattern (request, decide, event back to the originator) drives invoice approval, change requests, SLA exceptions, KPI targets and workflow gates.

Realtime updates

The Communication service also holds the WebSocket connections (Socket.IO) and pushes changes to users, so the UI never polls.

ChannelJoinedReceives
user:<id>Automatically on connectInbox items, approvals assigned, SLA warnings for your tasks, job completions, session revocation
subject:<type>:<id>subscribe message (authorized like a GET)Changes to that record while it is open on screen
unit:<id>subscribe (needs read scope on the unit)Team boards: task created, assigned, completed
  • Messages are hints to refetch, not a source of truth: always read the record through the REST API.
  • The server sends auth.expiring 60 seconds before the token expires; answer with reauth, otherwise the socket closes with code 4001.
  • Reconnect with exponential backoff. After a reconnect, refetch what is on screen; events missed while offline are not replayed beyond 5 minutes (resume with the last event id).

Webhooks

External systems can subscribe to FBOS events (create a subscription). Each delivery is the event envelope, signed with the subscription's secret.

  • Signature: v1= + hex HMAC-SHA256 of <timestamp>.<raw body> with the subscription secret.
  • Reject deliveries whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes old; de-duplicate on FBOS-Webhook-Id.
  • Answer 2xx within 10 seconds and process asynchronously. Anything else is retried after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h.
  • A subscription failing for 24 hours is disabled and its owner notified.
  • Outbound webhooks use the same relay, signing and retry schedule as internal event delivery between FBOS services.

Inbound webhooks

Provider webhooks (Razorpay today) are verified before the body is parsed, stored in an inbox keyed by the provider's event id (so redeliveries are ignored), acknowledged immediately, and processed asynchronously.

File uploads

Files never pass through FBOS services, which keeps them fast and lets uploads go up to 100 MB.

  • Declare the SHA-256 as hex in step 1; send it base64-encoded in the storage header (the upload headers are provided for you).
  • Complete the upload within one hour, otherwise 410 UPLOAD_EXPIRED.
  • Downloads are refused until the scan is clean (409 DOCUMENT_SCAN_PENDING, retryable). Download links are valid for 60 seconds and every access is logged.
  • To add a new version, send document_id in step 1. Approved versions lock the document.

Versioning and deprecation

ChangeBreaking?How it ships
New endpoint, new optional request field, new response field, new enum value, new event typeNoReleased any time. Clients must tolerate unknown fields and values.
Removing or renaming a field, changing a type or meaning, making an optional field required, new required headerYesOnly in a new major version (/v2) running alongside /v1.
Deprecating an endpoint—Deprecation and Sunset headers at least 6 months before removal; clients identified via X-Client-Version are contacted.
Event payload breaking changeYesPublish .v2 alongside .v1 until every consumer has migrated.

Issue an invoice

POST/api/revenue/v1/invoices/{invoice_id}/issue

In one transaction: takes the next gapless number from the GSTIN's series for the financial year, freezes the client snapshot and makes the invoice immutable. If the amount crosses the approval threshold, the call fails with APPROVAL_REQUIRED and the approval request id in meta; issue again after approval.

Permission
billing.invoice.issue
Authentication
Access token
Idempotency
Required: send Idempotency-Key
Concurrency
Send If-Match with the current ETag
Rate limit class
standard

  • If-Matchstringheaderrequired

    Defaults to today (organization timezone). Cannot be in the future or in a closed period.

Response

200 OK with Invoice.

What happens next
  • Document renders and stores the PDF (a few seconds).
  • For e-invoice-mandated entities, billing requests the IRN from the IRP; e_invoice fills in asynchronously.
  • Notification emails the invoice to the chosen contacts.
  • Performance records revenue_billed; planning records budget actuals.
  • Billing queues the Tally export.

Reveal a stored credential

POST/api/assets/v1/credentials/{credential_id}/reveal

Requires a credential grant and step-up authentication: the access token must be less than 5 minutes old from an MFA sign-in, or the request must carry X-MFA-Code. The value is fetched from the secret manager, never stored in FBOS databases, and every reveal is audited.

Permission
asset.credential.reveal
Authentication
Access token
Idempotency
Not applicable
Concurrency
—
Rate limit class
sensitive

    Credential id. Example: 0191f3a2-0059-7059-826f-0000008e39b1
  • X-MFA-Codestringheaderoptional
    Fresh TOTP code for step-up authentication.
Request body CredentialReveal
  • reasonstringrequired
Response

200 OK with CredentialSecret.

Events published

asset.credential.revealed.v1

Errors
HTTPCodeWhen it happens
403STEP_UP_REQUIREDSensitive action and the session's MFA is older than 5 minutes.

Also the standard errors for authentication (401), permission (403), not found (404), malformed or invalid input (400, 422), rate limiting (429) and server and dependency failures (500, 503). How to handle them.

Common to every service

Endpoints every service implements: health, and the internal event-delivery contract used instead of a message broker. Path pattern /api/{service}/v1.

Every service

Receive an event (internal delivery)

POST/api/{service}/v1/internal/events

Every service implements this endpoint. The producing service's outbox relay POSTs each event here. Answer 200 only after the event's effects are committed. Duplicates (same event_id) and stale versions are acknowledged with 200 so they are not retried. A 4xx other than 408/409/429 means the event can never be processed: the delivery is marked dead and alerted. A 5xx, 408, 429 or timeout (10 s) is retried.

Permission
None
Authentication
Internal service token (not public)
Idempotency
Not applicable
Concurrency
—
Rate limit class
internal
Parameters
  • servicestringpathrequired
    Service name. Example: delivery
  • X-FBOS-Event-Idstringheaderrequired
    Same as event_id in the body; lets proxies and logs de-duplicate.
  • X-FBOS-Event-Typestringheaderrequired
    Same as event_type in the body.
  • X-FBOS-Delivery-Attemptstringheaderrequired
    1 for the first attempt, then 2, 3… on retries.
Request body EventEnvelope
  • event_idstring (uuid)required
    Unique id; consumers de-duplicate on it.
  • event_typestringrequired
    <module>.<entity>.<verb>.v<major>
  • occurred_atstring (date-time)required
  • organization_idstring (uuid)required
  • actorobjectrequired
  • subjectobjectrequired
  • correlation_idstring (uuid)required
    Ties a whole business journey together.
  • causation_idstring (uuid)optional, nullable
    Event or request that directly caused this one.
  • scopeobjectrequired
  • payloadobjectrequired
Response

200 OK with EventAck.

Errors

Also the standard errors for malformed or invalid input (400, 422), rate limiting (429) and server and dependency failures (500, 503). How to handle them.

Error codes

Stable codes returned in problem.code. Program against these, never against the message text.

CodeHTTPTitleWhen it happensWhat the client should doRetry
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED400Idempotency-Key header is requiredThe endpoint moves money or records a decision and the header is missing.Generate a UUID per user action and send it; reuse it on retries.no
MALFORMED_REQUEST400Request body is not valid JSONThe body cannot be parsed, or a value has the wrong JSON type.Fix the request; do not retry unchanged.no
AUTH_REQUIRED401Authentication requiredNo Authorization header (or cookie) was sent.Sign in and send the access token.no
CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_INVALID401Client authentication failedUnknown client_id, wrong secret or disabled API client.Check integration credentials.no
INVALID_CREDENTIALS401Email or password is incorrectUnknown email or wrong password (deliberately indistinguishable).Show a generic message; offer password reset.no
INVITATION_INVALID401Invitation is invalid or expiredToken unknown, used or older than 72 hours.Ask an administrator to resend the invitation.no
MFA_CODE_INVALID401The verification code is incorrectWrong or reused TOTP code.Let the user try again (max 5 attempts per mfa_token).no
MFA_TOKEN_EXPIRED401Sign-in step expiredThe 5-minute mfa_token expired.Restart sign-in.no
REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID401Session expiredRefresh token missing, expired (30 days) or revoked.Sign in again.no
REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED401Session revoked for securityAn already-rotated refresh token was presented; the whole session family is revoked.Sign in again; the user receives a security email.no
RESET_TOKEN_INVALID401Reset link is invalid or expiredToken unknown, used or older than 30 minutes.Request a new reset email.no
SHARE_PASSWORD_REQUIRED401Password requiredPassword-protected share without (or with a wrong) X-Share-Password.Prompt for the password.no
TOKEN_EXPIRED401Access token expiredThe JWT exp is in the past (tokens live 15 minutes).Call /auth/token/refresh once, then retry the original request.yes
TOKEN_INVALID401Access token is invalidBad signature, unknown kid, wrong issuer/audience, or revoked session.Discard tokens and sign in again.no
WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID401Webhook signature is invalidHMAC signature does not match the raw body.Provider-side: check the webhook secret.no
ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE403Account is not activeThe user is invited, suspended or deactivated.Direct the user to their administrator.no
CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID403CSRF check failedX-CSRF-Token does not match the fbos_csrf cookie on a cookie-authenticated call.Reload the app to get a fresh CSRF cookie.no
NOT_AN_APPROVER403You are not an approver for this stepCaller is not a pending assignee of the active step (nor their delegate).Open your approval inbox.no
NOT_ASSIGNEE403Only the assignee can do thisStart/submit by someone other than the assignee.Reassign the task first.no
NOT_REVIEWER403Only the reviewer can review this taskCaller is not the reviewer and lacks review permission in scope.Ask the assigned reviewer.no
PERMISSION_DENIED403You don't have permission for this actionThe record is visible to you but your roles in its scope don't include the required permission.Show the message; request access from an administrator.no
SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED403You can't approve your own requestRequester equals approver and the policy forbids self-approval.The request routes to the next approver.no
STEP_UP_REQUIRED403Recent multi-factor authentication requiredSensitive action and the session's MFA is older than 5 minutes.Ask for a TOTP code and resend with X-MFA-Code.no
NOT_FOUND404Resource not foundThe id does not exist, or exists outside every scope you are granted. FBOS does not reveal which.Check the id; refresh lists that may be stale.no
ROUTE_NOT_FOUND404No such endpointPath or version does not match any route at the gateway.Check the URL and API version.no
METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED405Method not allowedThe path exists but not for this HTTP method.Use a documented method.no
ALREADY_DECIDED409You already decided on this stepSecond decision by the same assignee.Refetch the request.no
APPROVAL_REQUIRED409Approval required before issuingThe invoice crosses the approval threshold; an approval request was created.Issue again after the request is approved (meta.approval_request_id).no
ASSET_ALREADY_ASSIGNED409Asset is already assignedSingle-custodian assets can have one active assignment.Return the asset first.no
BASELINE_CHANGE_REQUIRES_CR409Change needs an approved change requestBaseline dates/budget can't change directly after approval.Raise a change request.no
CAPACITY_EXCEEDED409Allocation overloads this personAllocated minutes would exceed capacity on some days.Reduce minutes, change dates, or override with a reason.no
DELEGATION_OVERLAP409Delegation overlaps an existing oneTwo delegations for the same user overlap in time.Edit or end the existing delegation.no
DEPENDENCIES_OPEN409Blocking tasks are not finishedA finish-to-start dependency is still open.Finish the listed tasks first (meta.open_dependencies).no
DEPENDENCY_CYCLE409This dependency would create a loopThe new dependency makes the graph cyclic.Remove the conflicting dependency.no
DOCUMENT_INFECTED409File failed the virus scanMalware detected; the file is quarantined.Upload a clean file.no
DOCUMENT_LOCKED409Document is lockedAn approved version locks the document against new versions.Ask the owner to unlock or create a new document.no
DOCUMENT_SCAN_PENDING409File is still being scannedVirus scan not finished (usually under 30 seconds).Retry after a few seconds or wait for the realtime event.yes
DUPLICATE_CLIENT409This client already existsSame GSTIN, PAN or email domain as an existing client.Use the existing client (meta.existing_client_id).no
DUPLICATE_CODE409Code already existsA record with the same code exists in this organization.Choose another code.no
DUPLICATE_OPEN_REQUEST409An open request already exists for this objectOnly one open approval (or draft target) per subject and type.Open the existing request (meta.existing_id).no
EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS409A user with this email already existsEmails are unique per organization.Open the existing user instead.no
FIELD_NOT_EDITABLE_IN_STATUS409Field can't change in this statusFor example changing estimate after completion.Refetch and edit allowed fields only.no
HANDOVER_ALREADY_OPEN409A handover is already pending for this objectOnly one open handover per subject.Wait for the pending handover to be answered.no
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE409A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processedA retry arrived while the first attempt is still running.Wait 1–2 seconds and retry with the same key.yes
INSTANCE_ALREADY_RUNNING409A workflow is already running for this objectOne running instance per definition and subject.Open the existing instance (meta.instance_id).no
INSTANCE_NOT_RUNNING409Workflow is not runningInstance is on hold, waiting for approval, completed or cancelled.Refetch the instance.no
INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION409Action not allowed in the current statusThe state machine does not allow this action from the record's current status.Refetch the record and show the actions allowed now.no
INVOICE_NOT_DRAFT409Only draft invoices can be issuedThe invoice is already issued or cancelled.Refetch the invoice.no
INVOICE_NOT_PAYABLE409Invoice can't receive paymentsInvoice is draft, cancelled, fully paid or written off.Allocate to another invoice.no
ORGANIZATION_AMBIGUOUS409Choose an organizationThe email exists in several organizations.Ask for the organization code and retry.no
PERIOD_CLOSED409Accounting period is closedThe issue date falls in a closed period.Use a date in an open period or ask finance to reopen.no
QUOTATION_EXPIRED409Quotation has expiredvalid_until is in the past.Create a revision with a new validity date.no
QUOTATION_NOT_ACCEPTED409Quotation has not been acceptedContracts can only be created from an accepted revision.Record acceptance first.no
QUOTATION_NOT_APPROVED409Quotation is not approved yetSending requires status approved.Wait for approval or check the approval request.no
QUOTATION_NOT_EDITABLE409Quotation can't be editedOnly draft revisions can change; sent revisions are frozen.Create a new revision.no
ROLE_IS_SYSTEM409System roles can't be changedAttempt to edit a built-in role.Create a custom role instead.no
STEP_NOT_ACTIVE409This step is not activeDeciding on a waiting or finished step.Refetch the request.no
TASK_CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE409Mandatory checklist items are not doneSubmit attempted with unchecked mandatory items.Tick the listed items (meta.pending_items), then submit.no
TIME_ENTRY_LOCKED409Timesheet period is lockedThe week was approved and locked.Ask a manager to unlock.no
TRANSITION_CONDITION_FAILED409Transition conditions are not metThe JSON Logic condition evaluated to false.Show meta.blocked_reasons to the user.no
TRANSITION_NOT_AVAILABLE409Transition not available from the current stageUnknown code, or not an outgoing transition of the active stage.List available transitions first.no
VERSION_NOT_DRAFT409Only draft versions can be changedThe version is published or retired.Create a new draft version.no
WORK_UNIT_HAS_OPEN_ITEMS409Work unit still has open itemsClosing with open tasks, risks, change requests or incomplete milestones.Resolve the listed items (meta.open_items).no
SHARE_EXPIRED410This link has expiredShare expired, was revoked or hit its download limit.Ask the sender for a new link.no
UPLOAD_EXPIRED410Upload session expiredComplete was called after the 1-hour upload window.Start a new upload.no
VERSION_CONFLICT412The record was changed by someone elseIf-Match does not equal the record's current version.Refetch, show what changed, let the user re-apply the edit.no
FILE_TOO_LARGE413File is too largeExceeds 100 MB or the category limit.Compress or split the file.no
PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE413Request body too largeJSON bodies are limited to 1 MB (files use presigned uploads).Reduce the payload.no
MIME_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED415File type not allowedThe category doesn't accept this MIME type.Upload an allowed type.no
UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE415Unsupported content typeContent-Type is not application/json (or form-urlencoded where documented).Send JSON with Content-Type: application/json.no
ALLOCATION_EXCEEDS_BALANCE422Allocation exceeds invoice balanceAn allocation is larger than the invoice's balance due.Allocate at most the balance due.no
ALLOCATION_EXCEEDS_PAYMENT422Allocations exceed the paymentSum of allocations > amount + TDS.Reduce allocations.no
ASSIGNEE_NOT_IN_UNIT422Assignee is not a member of the owning teamTasks are team-owned; the assignee must belong to the unit.Pick a member or hand over the task.no
CHECKSUM_MISMATCH422Uploaded file doesn't match its checksumSHA-256 or size of the stored object differs from the declared values.Upload again.no
CLIENT_REQUIRED422A client is required for this work typeThe work unit type requires client_id.Provide client_id.no
COMMENT_REQUIRED422A comment is requiredReject and request_revision need a reason.Add a comment.no
CURRENCY_MISMATCH422Currency mismatchPayment/lines use a different currency than the invoice or contract.Use the document currency.no
DAILY_MINUTES_EXCEEDED422More than 24 hours logged for the daySum of the user's minutes for work_date would exceed 1440.Correct the entry.no
FEEDBACK_REQUIRED422Feedback is required when a review failsresult=fail without feedback.Add feedback.no
FIELD_SCHEMA_INVALID422Custom field schema is invalidNot valid JSON Schema 2020-12, or it removes a field still in use.Fix the schema; see errors[].no
GSTIN_INVALID422GSTIN is invalidWrong format, bad checksum, or state code doesn't match the address.Correct the GSTIN.no
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH422Idempotency-Key was used with a different requestSame key, different body or path.Generate a new key for a different action.no
KPI_NOT_MANUAL422This KPI can't take manual valuesThe KPI is fed by business events.Correct the source data instead.no
NO_APPROVAL_POLICY422No approval policy appliesNo active policy matches and the organization requires one.Ask an administrator to configure a policy.no
ORG_UNIT_CYCLE422A unit can't be moved under its own descendantThe new parent is inside the unit's subtree.Choose a parent outside the unit.no
ORG_UNIT_HIERARCHY_INVALID422This unit type can't be placed thereFor example a team directly under a company.Choose a valid parent type.no
PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK422Password doesn't meet the policyShorter than 12 characters or found in breached-password lists.Choose a longer, unique password.no
PAYMENT_TERMS_INVALID422Payment terms are invalidPercentages don't total 100, or a milestone code doesn't exist in the template.Fix the terms (see errors[]).no
RRULE_INVALID422Recurrence rule is invalidNot a valid RFC 5545 RRULE, or it produces no occurrences.Fix the rule.no
SAME_UNIT422From and to teams are the sameHandover to the same unit.Choose another receiving team.no
SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND422The linked business object was not foundsubject.type is unknown, or the object does not exist or is not visible to you.Check subject type and id.no
SUBJECT_TYPE_MISMATCH422Workflow doesn't apply to this object typedefinition.subject_type differs from subject.type.Choose a matching definition.no
TEMPLATE_INVALID422Template structure is invalidStructure fails the template JSON Schema.Fix the structure (see errors[]).no
TEMPLATE_NOT_PUBLISHED422Template has no published versionThe requested template (or version) is not published.Publish the template or pick another.no
VALIDATION_FAILED422Some fields are invalidSchema or field-level business rules failed.Highlight each entry in errors[] next to its field.no
VERTICAL_PACK_INVALID422Vertical pack manifest is invalidUnknown references or version conflicts in the manifest.Fix the manifest.no
WORKFLOW_VERSION_INVALID422Workflow version is invalidPublish-time validation failed.Fix the issues in errors[].no
ACCOUNT_LOCKED423Account temporarily lockedFive failed sign-ins within 15 minutes.Tell the user when they can try again (meta.locked_until).no
PRECONDITION_REQUIRED428If-Match header is requiredThe endpoint updates a versioned record and If-Match is missing.Send the ETag you received with the record.no
RATE_LIMITED429Too many requestsThe caller exceeded the rate-limit class for this endpoint.Wait for Retry-After seconds, then retry.yes
INTERNAL_ERROR500Unexpected errorA bug or unhandled failure. It is logged with the request id and alerts on-call.Retry once if the request is idempotent; otherwise report the request_id.yes
DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE503A required service is temporarily unavailableA downstream service, database or provider is unreachable and the circuit breaker is open.Retry after Retry-After with the same Idempotency-Key.yes
UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT504The request took too longThe service did not answer within the route's timeout budget.Retry with the same Idempotency-Key; the first attempt may have succeeded.yes
